title: Libraries reinvent themselves
passage: For years, the library's role was taken for granted. Then the Internet arrived, and many predicted the printed book would become obsolete. Yet the opposite happened: libraries reinvented themselves as community hubs — offering courses, co-working space, and free access to digital archives. The institution did not vanish; it adapted, and in adapting it found a new reason to exist.

vocab.example: We take clean water for granted until it runs out.
Typewriters became obsolete once computers spread.
She reinvented herself as a novelist.
The old shops vanished from the high street.
Small firms adapt to change faster than big ones.

options.text: 图书馆终将被互联网淘汰
图书馆转型重生，找到了新角色
互联网让纸质书变得过时
数字档案馆比实体图书馆更受欢迎

quiz.explanation: 末句 found a new reason to exist 与段首形成对照，说明图书馆不是消失而是转型。

quiz.stem: 文中 obsolete 在这里最接近哪个意思？
quiz.explanation: obsolete 指被新事物取代而淘汰，与互联网预言纸质书'被淘汰'的语境吻合。
the opposite 与前半句 many predicted... 相对，指与预言相反的情况——图书馆没有被淘汰。

quiz.stem: 第二句与第三句之间的逻辑关系是？
quiz.explanation: Yet 是转折信号词，表示实际情况与上一句的预言相反。

translation.instructions: 把下面的句子译成中文，先自己译，再展开参考。

items.source: The institution did not vanish; it adapted, and in adapting it found a new reason to exist.
items.reference: 这个机构并没有消失；它适应了变化，并在适应过程中找到了新的存在理由。
points: in adapting 译出「在适应过程中」

items.source: Yet the opposite happened: libraries reinvented themselves as community hubs.
items.reference: 然而，情况恰恰相反：图书馆把自身重新打造为社区中心。
points: the opposite 指与预言相反的情况
reinvented themselves as 译出「把自身重新打造为」
